findings.title: `float: right` on `.small-action button` is a no-op once `.small-action` becomes a flex container
findings.body: `.small-action` is now `display: flex` (via `@include flexbox()`), which makes `.topic-avatar`, `.small-action-desc` and `button` flex items. Per the flexbox spec `float` has no effect on flex items, so the existing `button { float: right; }` no longer pushes the edit/delete buttons to the right edge; they will render immediately after the description text. Nothing else in the rule (no `margin-left: auto` on the button, no `flex: 1` on `.small-action-desc`) compensates for this, so the small-action rows lose their right-aligned controls. Either add `margin-left: auto` to the button or `flex: 1` to `.small-action-desc`.

findings.title: `align-items` mixin passes modern keywords straight to legacy IE10/old-WebKit properties
findings.body: The mixin emits `-ms-flex-align: $alignment` and `-webkit-box-align: $alignment` with the unmodified argument. The legacy syntaxes use `start`/`end`, not `flex-start`/`flex-end`, so any future call such as `@include align-items(flex-start)` will silently produce invalid declarations in IE10 and old WebKit/Android while appearing to work elsewhere. The current callers only pass `center` and `baseline` (which happen to be shared keywords), but the mixin's contract is misleading. Additionally `-ms-align-items` (line 121) is not a real property in any browser and is dead output.

findings.title: Legacy `-webkit-box` fallback does not support the `margin-left: auto` layout relied on in the header
findings.body: The `flexbox()` mixin emits `display: -webkit-box` as the fallback for old WebKit (Android 2.x–4.3 stock browser, Safari <6.1). In the 2009 box model, `margin: auto` on children is not treated as free-space distribution, so the `.d-header .panel { margin-left: auto }` introduced in header.scss will not push the panel to the right on those browsers; it will sit directly after the title/extra-info. Previously the panel was `float: right`, which worked everywhere. If those browsers are still supported, the panel needs an alternative (e.g. `-webkit-box-flex: 1` on a spacer or on `.title`), otherwise the legacy prefixes are just misleading.

findings.title: Removing the bullet margin-top fix leaves `.badge-wrapper.box` in the header offset by 5px
findings.body: The diff removes `.extra-info-wrapper .badge-wrapper.bullet { margin-top: 5px }` on the assumption that `align-items: center` on `.d-header .contents` now vertically centres badges. However `badges.css.scss` still sets `.badge-wrapper.box { margin-top: 5px }` globally (line 101), which in a centred flex row shifts box-style category badges 5px below the centre line while bullet and bar styles are centred. Sites using the box badge style will see a misaligned category badge in the header; the box margin should be overridden inside `.extra-info-wrapper` the same way the bullet one was handled.

findings.title: PR title claims a performance optimisation; the change is a layout refactor with visible behavioural changes and the description is a placeholder
findings.body: The PR is titled "Optimize header layout performance with flexbox mixins" and described only as "Test 5". Switching from floats to flexbox is not a performance optimisation and the diff intentionally changes rendering: header items are reordered via `order`, `.small-action-desc` padding changes from `0.5em 0 0.5em 4em` to `0 1.5%`, and paragraph margins/padding inside small actions are removed. Reviewers and future readers of the history will be misled about intent and risk; the title/description should accurately describe the layout changes and their expected visual impact.
